full_judgment:
2. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and other dated 21.08.2011 passed by the High. Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal No.196 of 2011 allowing the appeal with cost of Tk. 50,000/- and setting aside the order dated 27.04.2011 passed by the learned Joint Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.31 of 2011 directing the defendants to maintain status quo for a period of 6 (six) months and prohibiting from taking any step in respect of the suit cold storage. 

 6. Thereafter, respondent Nos.1 and 2 as the appellants filed First Miscellaneous Appeal No.196 of 2011 against the order dated 27.04.2011 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Fifth Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No.31 of 2011 for maintaining the order of status quo for six months. Appellant-respondent No.1 and 2 also filed an application for stay of the operation of the above mentioned order. The High Court Division admitted the appeal and after hearing the application for stay issued rule and stayed the operation of the order impugned before it and the same was registered as Civil Rule No. 479 (EM.) of 2011. 

 9. Mr. A. M. Aminuddin, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioner, submits that the petitioner passed an order of injunction in Title Suit No.31 of 2011 which is a judicial order and that the High Court Division without considering this aspect of the case directed to send the judgment of First Miscellaneous Appeal to the Ministry of law for evaluation of his judicial function as evident from the impugned judgment and order. The judicial functions cannot be evaluated by the Administrative Authority and this is a clear violation of Article 116A of the Constitution and therefore, the adverse remarks/ observations made against the leave petitioner should be expunged. He further submits that the adverse remarks were passed without providing the leave petitioner any opportunity of being heard and are violative of the principles of natural justice and as such, the High Court Division committed gross error of law in passing the adverse remarks against the Judge-leave-petitioner. 

 12. The High Court Division, however, made some adverse comments against the Judge, who has passed the order impugned before it. From this Division, we are saying time and again that no adverse comment should be passed against anybody particularly in case of judicial officer without giving him an opportunity of being heard. It is well settled principle of natural justice that no one should be condemned unheard. In addition, strictures or scathing Language should not be used by the higher Courts in exercise of their appellate or supervisory jurisdiction against the Judges of the lower Courts. Errors of the judgments should be corrected by reasons of Law. 

 13. In the case in hand, the High Court Division has passed the following adverse comment the judicial officers, who have passed the order impugned before it. The adverse comments are: "Hence, the impugned order is not only illegal, but it raises the ability of this particular Judge to try a case and about his possessing elementary knowledge of Laws that are applicable in most of the civil proceedings." 

 "Let a copy of the judgment and order be sent to the Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, for their evaluation of the judicial function of the learned Judge, Mr. Mohammad Sharif Hossain Hayder and another copy of the judgment be also sent to his controlling officer to see if similar orders were passed in any other cases and to evaluate his overall performance as a judicial officer. Let a copy of the judgment be sent to the learned Register of the Supreme Court for record." 

 17. In this connection reliance may be placed on the case of P. Sathasivam, J. in Manu Sharma v. State (NCT of Delhi), (2010) 6 SCC 1. In that case, it has been held as under: 

 18. From the case referred to above, it appears that errors of judgments should be corrected by reasons of law and that the practice of passing comments against lower courts is not at all proper.
